quote: (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid.
rationale: Section 4 runs in our favour and meets the preferred position on its material terms. All work product prepared for Clear Capital under a SOW ("Works") is the property of Company (paid-for work), with Contractor obliged to give assistance and execute documents to perfect those rights (p0017-p0018). Contractor retains only its own pre-existing tools, methodologies and know-how not created for us (p0020), and grants us a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivatives of any Contractor Information embedded in the Works for our business operations (p0021), plus an express right after payment to modify the software or engage third parties to do so without further fees (p0022). Nothing assigns or licenses Clear Capital IP or Clear Capital data to Contractor, and no joint ownership is created; § 5(b) expressly carves out programs, data and materials provided by Company from Contractor's granting rights. Minor sub-elements short of the ideal, noted but not flagged: there is no separate "Customer Data" ownership sentence (our data is instead protected as Confidential Information in § 8), ownership is expressed as vesting rather than a present assignment of copyright, further-assurance assistance is at our cost, and the licence-back is not labelled irrevocable or worldwide. These do not affect the substance of our ownership or exploitation rights, so no redline.

rationale: The Agreement contains no exclusivity, sole-supplier, minimum-commitment, requirements or right-of-first-refusal obligation on Clear Capital. Engagement is on a task-by-task basis via Statements of Work (p0004), leaving us free to retain other suppliers. The only uses of "exclusive" are IP/property-related (Contractor's ownership of its own pre-existing materials at p0020 and the non-exclusive license grant to Company at p0021) and the entire-agreement clause (p0051) — none restricts our freedom to purchase elsewhere. quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-damages, early-termination or minimum-fee obligation payable by Clear Capital. Compensation (§ 3) is pure time-and-materials with no minimum commitment and no late-payment penalty or interest; termination (§ 6(a)/(b) and the duplicated § 7(c)) entitles the Contractor only to fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the termination date, which is compensatory rather than a stipulated sum, and § 5 even relieves Company of any fee obligation on certain terminations. The mutual liability cap in § 7(a) limits, rather than creates, Company-payable damages. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted. We note only that any Statement of Work should be checked to ensure it does not introduce a cancellation or minimum-hours fee, which would need to be capped at three months' fees under the fallback.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The only licence grant to us is § 4(c) (p0021), covering Contractor's Information embedded in the Works. It meets the preferred position on the material terms: the licence is perpetual and royalty-free with no revocation right reserved to Contractor (nothing makes it revocable at Contractor's discretion or terminable other than for the express contract remedies), it is broad in scope ("in connection with Company's business operations", including modification and derivative works), and it includes an unrestricted right to grant sublicences, which gives us a path to extend use to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf without notice or consent — better than the fallback (affiliates on written notice). § 4(d) (p0022) reinforces this by letting us engage third parties to modify the software. Non-exclusivity is expected for a vendor's background IP and is not a concern. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal wording and are noted rather than flagged: the grant does not say "irrevocable" expressly, and successor transfer runs through the mutual assignment clause (p0042), which requires consent that "will not be unreasonably withheld" rather than a carve-out for M&A successors — that assignment mechanic is addressed under the assignment rule and is not double-flagged here. No walk-away features (no vendor-discretionary revocation, no exclusion of affiliates/contractors).

rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Clear Capital. I reviewed the scope/purpose provisions (§ 1), the IP and acceptance provisions (§ 4), warranties (§ 5), termination (§ 6) and the miscellaneous/surviving covenants (§ 7), and searched for competing-product, exclusivity, field-of-use and "shall not develop/market/sell" language. The only restrictions on Company are (i) § 4(b)(ii)'s limit on reselling or using Contractor's own background IP outside the software Company receives, which is an IP-scope limitation rather than a restraint on our business, and (ii) the mutual one-year employee non-solicit in § 13, which is a hiring restriction addressed under the non-solicitation rule, not a non-compete. ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend and indemnify Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses, to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any data breach or unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of any such claim and reasonable cooperation in the defense, and Contractor shall have control of the defense. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c).

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor," but the section contains only liability caps (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys' fees waiver (7(c)) — a full-text search for "indemn" returns only the heading, so no operative indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement in either direction. That fails even the fallback: there is no Vendor IP indemnity, no defence obligation, and no remedy for third-party infringement claims. The 5(c) IP non-infringement warranty is not a substitute, because a warranty carries no duty to defend or to fund our costs, and any resulting claim would be squeezed into the 7(a) cap of fees paid (with 7(c) forcing us to bear our own attorneys' fees). The 7(a) cross-reference to "Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9" appears to be a drafting error, since Paragraph 9 is Independent Contractor status, not an indemnity. We inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused disclosure of Confidential Information, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics as new 7(d), carved out of the Section 7 limitations, and conformed the heading. No Customer indemnity exists to narrow. A 3x annual fees super-cap on these obligations is available as a fallback.

verification.notes: All preferred atomic elements are present in operative language: defend and indemnify, Customer plus affiliates, and all four coverage triggers (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct). Procedure is limited to the three permitted mechanics (notice, control, cooperation); no hold-harmless, no Customer defence duty, no added indemnitees, no settlement-consent mechanics. The conditional Customer-indemnity limitation is satisfied because no Customer indemnity exists in the clause or document; none was invented. The insertion is a concise new subsection for an absent clause; the carve-out from Sections 7(a)-(c) is necessary to avoid a dangling contradiction with the existing fees-paid cap and the mutual attorneys'-fees waiver, and does not rewrite the untouched liability provisions. Fallback is not met (no usual exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but the locked target is preferred and the two levels are not combined; the available super-cap is correctly offered only in the non-operative comment. quote: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: This rule is directional: it is triggered only where the Customer must extend to the Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, or must match third-party offers. The compensation provisions in § 3 set pricing solely by reference to each Statement of Work on a time-and-materials basis (with a Contractor-side right to change rates on 30 days' notice, addressed under the pricing/uplift rules rather than here). Searches across the full agreement for "most favoured", "most favored", "favorable", "no less" and third-party comparison language return no most-favoured-nation, most-favoured-customer, benchmarking or rate-matching mechanic anywhere in the document, and the only sections present (§§ 1, 3–7) contain no such construct. There is therefore no MFN obligation burdening Clear Capital, which is the playbook's preferred position — the absence of the clause is the outcome we want, so this is compliant rather than "missing" and no redline is warranted. Noted for completeness only: the agreement likewise grants us no MFN pricing in our favour, which would be welcome but is an upside ask, not a deviation under this rule.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, guaranteed spend, guaranteed hours, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, exclusivity or volume restriction on Clear Capital. Engagement is expressly "on a task by task basis" under mutually agreed Statements of Work (p0004), and compensation is time-and-materials for Services actually performed plus actual expenses (p0013). Termination for convenience is available whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding on 15 days' notice, and on breach the Contractor is paid only for fees "incurred or earned ... through the effective date of such termination" (p0032, p0033) — i.e., no early-termination or shortfall penalty. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "guarantee", "volume" and "quota" returned no Customer-side commitment language. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for ordered services only), so no redline is proposed. quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 13 binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. It already meets most of the fallback: it is mutual, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, runs only for the term plus one year, and is a solicitation restriction rather than a no-hire. However, it contains no carve-out for general advertisements/untargeted recruiting or for unsolicited approaches, which the rule treats as a required element of an acceptable non-solicit ("narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out"). Without it, ordinary hiring activity could breach the clause. The redline adds only the carve-out sentence, leaving duration and scope untouched, which brings the clause to the fallback position.

quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Contrary to the planner hint that no insurance clause exists, ¶14 (carried under sec-7) contains a full vendor insurance covenant binding Contractor for the term: workers' compensation at the statutory amount, commercial general liability of at least USD 1,000,000, and professional errors and omissions of at least USD 1,000,000, with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance on Company's request plus prompt written notice of any material change. This meets the fallback on its material terms (E&O USD 1M) and in fact matches the preferred position on workers' compensation, CGL per-occurrence limit and certificates-on-request, so it is not redlined. Two sub-elements fall short of preferred and are noted rather than flagged: the CGL aggregate (2M) and the E&O uplift to 2M are not stated. Cyber/privacy coverage is also absent, but the preferred position conditions cyber on vendors "processing Customer Data," and this is a task-by-task consulting engagement with no Customer Data definition, no hosting or SaaS element, and no personal-data processing anywhere in the document; §1(c) has Contractor performing Services at its own facility using its own computing equipment, with only incidental on-site presence and system access subject to Company's security policies, and §8 protects Company records and information through confidentiality obligations. The walk-away trigger (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data or working on our premises) is therefore not engaged. Given the low severity, we would raise cyber liability of at least USD 2,000,000 and the CGL aggregate/E&O uplift only if a Statement of Work later puts Contractor in a hosting role or gives it custody of personal data.

rationale: A mutual cap and a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages exist (p0035, p0036), so the structure is not one-sided against us. However, the cap fails the fallback on carve-outs: the only exception is "CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9", and Paragraph 9 is "INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR" — there is no indemnification clause anywhere in the agreement (the sole hit for "indemnif" is the Section 7 heading), so the carve-out is inoperative. Nothing is carved out for confidentiality (Section 8), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement (the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty is fully capped). The fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct, so this is a material failure. The basis is also weaker than preferred: fees "PAID" (not paid or payable) for the individual Statement of Work, which can fall well below twelve months' fees, with no USD floor. We left Company's cap untouched because it limits our exposure and benefits us. Redline sets Contractor's cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, defines Excluded Claims as uncapped, and confirms our fee-payment obligation is not "damages".

quote: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
rationale: There is no auto-renewal in this Agreement: § 2 (p0011) makes the term evergreen ("shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and § 6(a) lets either party exit for convenience on fifteen (15) days' notice when no Statement of Work is outstanding. The rule's second material limb — predictable renewal/roll-over pricing — fails, however: § 3(b) gives Contractor an uncapped unilateral right to change rates on 30 days' notice, with no annual frequency limit and no protection for work already under an outstanding Statement of Work (precisely the period when Company cannot use the § 6(a) convenience exit). We therefore cap increases at the lesser of CPI and 3% (preferred; 5% is our fallback), limit them to once per twelve months, and carve out outstanding Statements of Work.

The same clause also gives Contractor an at-will exit on 15 days' notice, short of the fallback's 90-day, end-of-term-only Vendor right, though this is mitigated because Contractor may only use it when no Statement of Work is outstanding. Redline adds a 30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW with a refund of prepaid fees and no penalty, and conforms Contractor's residual at-will right to 90 days' notice between engagements.
